items.stem: A 10 mm long alpin is placed vertically in front of a concave mirror. A 5 mm long image of the alpin is formed at 30 cm in front of the mirror. The focal length of this mirror is

options.label: A
options.text: -30 cm

options.label: B
options.text: -20 cm

options.label: C
options.text: -40 cm

options.label: D
options.text: -60 cm

items.answer: (b) -20 cm. Magnification m = h'/h = 5/10 = 1/2, and the image is real (formed in front of the mirror), so m = -1/2 = -v/u with v = -30 cm, giving u = -60 cm. From the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f: 1/(-30) + 1/(-60) = -3/60 = -1/20, so f = -20 cm.

items.stem: A light ray enters from medium A to medium B as shown in Figure. The refractive index of medium B relative to A will be

options.text: greater than unity

options.label: B
options.text: less than unity

options.label: C
options.text: equal to unity

options.label: D

items.answer: (b) less than unity. The ray bends away from the normal on entering B, so B is optically rarer than A and n(BA) < 1.

items.stem: Beams of light are incident through the holes A and B and emerge out of box through the holes C and D respectively as shown in Figure. Which of the following could be inside the box?

options.label: A
options.text: A rectangular glass slab

options.label: B
options.text: A convex lens

options.label: C
options.text: A concave lens

options.label: D
options.text: A prism

items.answer: (a) A rectangular glass slab. The emergent beams stay parallel to the incident beams (only laterally displaced), which is the behaviour of a rectangular glass slab.

items.stem: A beam of light is incident through the holes on side A and emerges out of the holes on the other face of the box as shown in Figure. Which of the following could be inside the box?

options.text: Concave lens

options.label: B
options.text: Rectangular glass slab

options.label: C
options.text: Prism

options.label: D
options.text: Convex lens

items.answer: (d) Convex lens. The parallel beam entering side A converges on emerging, which only a converging (convex) lens can do.

items.stem: Magnification produced by a rear view mirror fitted in vehicles

options.label: A

options.text: is more than one

options.label: C
options.text: is equal to one

options.label: D

items.answer: (a) is less than one. A rear view mirror is convex and always forms a diminished, virtual, erect image, so m < 1.

items.stem: Rays from Sun converge at a point 15 cm in front of a concave mirror. Where should an object be placed so that size of its image is equal to the size of the object?

options.label: A
options.text: 15 cm in front of the mirror

options.label: B
options.text: 30 cm in front of the mirror

options.label: C
options.text: between 15 cm and 30 cm in front of the mirror

options.label: D
options.text: more than 30 cm in front of the mirror

items.answer: (b) 30 cm in front of the mirror. Sun's rays converge at the focus, so f = 15 cm and R = 2f = 30 cm. An object placed at the centre of curvature (30 cm) gives an image of the same size as the object.

items.stem: A full length image of a distant tall building can definitely be seen by using

options.label: A
options.text: a concave mirror

options.label: B
options.text: a convex mirror

options.label: C
options.text: a plane mirror

options.label: D
options.text: both concave as well as plane mirror

items.answer: (b) a convex mirror. A convex mirror always forms a highly diminished, virtual, erect image and has a very wide field of view, so the full length of a tall building can be seen in it.

items.stem: In torches, search lights and headlights of vehicles the bulb is placed

items.stem: In which of the following, the image of an object placed at infinity will be highly diminished and point sized?

options.text: Convex lens only

options.label: D

items.answer: (d) Concave mirror, convex mirror, concave lens and convex lens. For an object at infinity all four form a highly diminished, point-sized image at the focus.

items.stem: The laws of reflection hold good for

items.stem: A child is standing in front of magic mirror. She finds the image of her head bigger, the middle portion of her body of the same size and that of the legs smaller. The following is the order of combinations for the magic mirror from the top.

items.answer: (a) Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion. Refractive index of any medium is defined as the ratio of speed of light in air or vacuum to speed of light in the given medium. Since speed of light is maximum in air (as in vacuum), air is the rarest medium. Hence both assertion and reason are true.

items.stem: Assertion : For observing traffic at our back, we prefer to use a convex mirror. Reason : A convex mirror has a much larger field of view than a plane mirror or a concave mirror.
items.assertion: For observing traffic at our back, we prefer to use a convex mirror.
items.reason: A convex mirror has a much larger field of view than a plane mirror or a concave mirror.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

items.answer: (a) Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion. A convex mirror bends light as it reflects it, and the farther a point is from the centre the more the light is bent. As a result, an image formed in a convex mirror is smaller than the image in a plane (flat) mirror. Because the image is smaller, more images fit onto the mirror, so a convex mirror provides a larger field of view than a plane mirror. They are used wherever a mirror with a large field of view is needed to observe traffic.

items.stem: State a condition for no refraction of light when light enters from one medium to another.
items.answer: No refraction of light occurs when light is incident normally (at an angle of incidence of 0°) on the boundary of two media.

items.stem: Write the relation between refractive index and speed of light in the medium.
items.answer: Refractive index = (Velocity of light in vacuum) / (Velocity of light in medium), i.e. n = c/v.

items.stem: What is the cause of refraction?
items.answer: Refraction of a light ray is caused due to the change in velocity of light when it travels from one medium to another medium.

items.stem: "Refractive index of glass is 1.5." What does it mean by this statement?
items.answer: It means the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in glass is equal to 1.5.

items.stem: Write the lens formula.
items.answer: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, where u is the object distance, v the image distance and f the focal length of the lens.

items.stem: Is it possible to form a real image using a real object with a concave lens?
items.answer: No, a real image is not formed by a concave lens for a real object; a concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.

items.stem: In which direction, the ray of light bends as it travels from denser to rarer medium?
items.answer: The ray bends away from the normal when it travels from a denser to a rarer medium.

items.stem: What is the value of ₁n₂ × ₂n₁ ?
items.answer: ₁n₂ × ₂n₁ = (v₁/v₂) × (v₂/v₁) = 1.

items.stem: Define absolute refractive index of a medium.
items.answer: Absolute refractive index of a medium is the refractive index of that medium with respect to vacuum.

items.stem: What is the relation between emergent ray and incident ray when light ray passes through a rectangular glass slab?
items.answer: The emergent ray and the incident ray are parallel to each other (the emergent ray is only laterally displaced).

items.stem: Refractive index of water is 4/3 and for glass it is 3/2, with respect to air. What is the refractive index of glass with respect to water?
items.answer: wng = ng/nw = (3/2)/(4/3) = (3/2) × (3/4) = 9/8. Hence the refractive index of glass with respect to water is 9/8.

items.stem: What is meant by magnification in the context of image formation by mirror and lenses?
items.answer: The ratio of the size of the image to the size of the object is called magnification, m = hᵢ/h₀.

items.stem: Which property of concave mirror is utilised for using them as shaving mirror?
items.answer: When an object is placed between the pole and the focus of a concave mirror, a magnified, erect and virtual image is formed; this property is used in a shaving mirror.

items.stem: What are the values of angle of incidence and angle of reflection for the normal incidence?
items.answer: Angle of incidence, ∠i = 0° and angle of reflection, ∠r = 0°.

items.stem: Find the focal length of a convex mirror whose radius of curvature is 32 cm.
items.answer: Given, radius of curvature R = 32 cm. Since R = 2 × focal length, f = R/2 = 32/2 = 16 cm. Hence the focal length of the given convex mirror is 16 cm.
